measures.what: the width of the slot opening at the top surface
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.item: tripod head (the clamp/carriage the plate slides into)
measures.what: the width of the slot at its bottom (the widest point, inside)
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.item: tripod head (the clamp/carriage the plate slides into)
measures.what: the depth of the slot, from the top surface down to the slot floor
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.item: tripod head (the clamp/carriage the plate slides into)
measures.what: the length of the slot along the slide direction, and whether the slot is open at one/both ends or closed
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: its length from under the head to the tip, and whether the thread goes all the way to the head
measures.reply: webcam bolt head across: about 15 mm (its head); webcam bolt head height: about 5 mm (its head); webcam bolt length: about 10 mm (under the head)

measures.what: the diameter and height of its head, and what kind of head it is (hex, socket cap, thumb wheel, wingnut-style)
measures.reply: webcam bolt head across: about 15 mm (its head); webcam bolt head height: about 5 mm (its head)

measures.what: the depth of the 1/4"-20 tripod socket hole in its base
measures.reply: camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

measures.what: Are the two side walls of the slot undercut — i.e. do they lean out as they go down (dovetail, so the slot is narrower at the top than at the bottom), or are they straight/vertical? Try laying a small ruler or a credit card edge against the wall and see if the top edge overhangs.
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above; tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: the depth of the slot — measure from the flat top face of the clamp straight down to the floor of the slot, using the depth rod of the calipers or a pencil poked in and marked
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above; tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: the length of the slot in the direction the plate slides, and whether the slot runs right off both ends of the clamp (open) or is closed at the ends
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: whether there is a locking screw, knob or spring pin that presses against the plate — look/feel at the side and underside of the head — and roughly where it contacts the plate
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: how deep the threaded hole goes — push a toothpick or a bit of wire into it and mark it at the surface, then measure that (or use the caliper depth rod). I need this because the salvaged bolt only has ~10 mm of thread and I must not let it bottom out.
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above; tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes); camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

measures.what: what shape the ~15 mm head is when viewed from the top and from the side — a round knurled thumb knob, a hexagon, or wings — and whether its underside is flat or conical. This decides whether I can pocket it into the plate or must leave it proud.
measures.reply: webcam bolt head across: about 15 mm (its head); webcam bolt head height: about 5 mm (its head)

measures.what: the length of the opening a plate sits in — from the inside wall at one end to the inside wall at the other, i.e. how long a plate can be. If the slot runs out the front and/or back so a longer plate could overhang the end, please say so.
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: whether the floor of the slot (what the plate's underside would rest on) is flat, or has a raised pad, a screw head, a rubber pad or a spring pin sticking up in it
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.item: salvaged webcam-mount bolt, screwed into the camera
measures.what: screw it into the camera's tripod socket finger-tight, then measure how much threaded length is still sticking out below the camera's base. That tells me the most thread I can let protrude up into the socket without bottoming out.
measures.reply: webcam bolt length: about 10 mm (under the head); camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

measures.what: with the jaws loosened right off, the length of the opening in the direction the plate's long side would lie — hold the head so you look along the slot and measure the distance from the end wall to the other end wall (or confirm it is open at the ends)
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)

measures.what: is the floor of the slot flat and clear all the way along, or is there a rubber pad, a screw head or a small pin sticking up in it that a plate would sit on
measures.reply: tripod clamp plate width: 38 mm (the width of plate it takes)
